test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 26 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is true for an ionic compound?

options.text: In an ionic compound, the transfer of electrons takes place from a non-metal to a non-metal.
In an ionic compound, the transfer of electrons takes place from a non-metal to a metal.
In an ionic compound, the transfer of electrons takes place from a metal to a non-metal.
In an ionic compound, the transfer of electrons takes place from a metal to a metal.

solution:
The correct answer is __**In an ionic compound, the transfer of electrons takes place from a metal to a non-metal.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ionic compounds** are formed through the transfer of electrons from a metal to a non-metal.
 
• Metals tend to lose electrons and become **positively charged cations**.
 
• Non-metals tend to gain electrons and become **negatively charged anions**.
 
• The electrostatic attraction between the oppositely charged ions results in the formation of an ionic bond.
 
• An example of an ionic compound is **sodium chloride (NaCl)**, where sodium (metal) transfers an electron to chlorine (non-metal).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ionic Bond**

 
 
• A type of chemical bond where atoms transfer electrons to achieve a full valence shell.
 
• Typically occurs between elements with a large difference in electronegativity.
 
• Results in the formation of ions that attract each other to form a stable compound.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Ionic Compounds**
 
 
• High melting and boiling points due to strong electrostatic forces between ions.
 
• Good electrical conductivity in molten or aqueous states, but not in solid form.
 
• Generally soluble in water but insoluble in organic solvents.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Ionic Compounds**
 
 
• Sodium chloride (NaCl)
 
• Magnesium oxide (MgO)
 
• Calcium fluoride (CaF₂)
 
 
 
• **Formation of Ions**
 
 
• Metals lose electrons to achieve a stable noble gas configuration, forming cations.
 
• Non-metals gain electrons to achieve a stable noble gas configuration, forming anions.
 
• This transfer of electrons leads to the formation of an ionic bond.
